_comment: klt erc supply spec for the full 256x32 SRAM array GDS -- the artifact
klayout-tools' T1 item 11 (power delivery, structural)
docs/design-evidence-tiers.md grades for this block. This block is
ratified `analog` (spec/block-kind-decision.md), so item 11's Analog
column applies: this supply-spec run, plus item 4's own LVS report
having carried the supply nets in its net_correspondence, which it
does -- layout/reports/lvs-array.json pairs layout VDD->reference
VDD and layout VSS->reference VSS, both `pin: true`, against the
SPICE reference netlist (a SPICE reference carries the supplies by
construction, per item 11's own text).
Run it against the committed array GDS:
klt erc layout/sram_256x32/sram_256x32_array.gds \
layout/sram_256x32/erc-supply-spec.json --format json
What this spec asserts, and why each piece is shaped this way --
every layer/datatype claim below was read out of THIS repo's GDS, the
PDK's own libs.tech/klayout/tech/gf180mcu.lyp, and klt's curated
gf180mcu deck layer table, not copied from another PDK's spec (the
fleet's worked example gf180-drone-fc layout/digital/erc-supply-spec.json
is the shape precedent; this spec re-derives every number for this
block):
- stackup[0] MUST carry role "gate" (klt erc's own contract), so the
stack starts at Poly2. `active_layer` (Comp 22/0) computes true
gate area as poly INTERSECT diff (klayout-tools issue #1979): the
array's 256 wordline landing pads are widened Poly2 drawn OUTSIDE
any diffusion (layout/sram_256x32/generate.py's WL_PAD_* -- the pad
a contact needs but no gate oxide), so raw-poly gate area would
count real interconnect in the antenna denominator.
- The stackup stops at Metal3: this block draws nothing above 42/0.
Measured from the merged GDS, the layer inventory ends at
Metal3/Via2 (Metal4 46/0, Via3 40/0, Metal5 81/0 all carry zero
shapes -- also recorded by spec/pdk-variant-decision.md). Declaring
empty roles would add nothing; the stackup covers exactly the
layers the supply is routed on.
- Metal1 carries `label_layer` 34/10 because that is where this GDS
puts its 320 array-level port texts (measured: WL0..WL255,
BL0..BL31, BLB0..BLB31, one text each). This is NOT supply text:
this block is a hand-drawn full-custom array, not an abutted
standard-cell macro, so the "PG pin text lives on 34/10" convention
of a standard-cell flow does not apply here. The texts exist, so
the declaration is made: it names the wordline nets so the report's
per-gate antenna table is readable as WL<n> instead of gate<n>.
The supply grading itself never reads these labels -- VDD/VSS are
resolved from 42/10 text (below) and are declared in nets[], not
from anything on 34/10.
- Metal2 carries no `label_layer`: measured from the merged GDS,
36/10 has ZERO texts. The bitcell's own cell-level M2 supply
labels are deliberately suppressed in the array
(layout/sram_256x32/generate.py draws 8,192 placements
with_labels=False -- 8,192 copies of `VDD`/`VSS` texts would be
8,192 same-named texts on 256 per-row and 32 per-column physically
distinct M2 rail pieces).
- Metal3 carries `label_layer` 42/10 -- the ONE layer this GDS
actually puts supply text on (measured: exactly two texts, `VDD`
and `VSS`, on the two array-level straps). This is how nets[]
resolves each supply to its electrical island.
- Vias: Contact 33/0 bridges poly2->Metal1 (the WL landing pads'
contacts and the bitcell's cross-couple poly contacts). Contact
cuts landing on Comp connect to nothing in this read -- Comp is
declared as active_layer, not a stackup role, so the supply reads
on the metal graph only, never through a device channel. Via1
35/0 bridges the bitcell's M1 tie bars up to its M2 rails (the
VSS riser at the substrate tie bar, the VDD riser at the well tie
bar). Via2 38/0 lands the two Metal3 straps down onto those rails
(measured: 64 cuts, two per column across all 32 columns).
- nets[]: VDD and VSS both kind "supply" -- which is what makes a
short between them report as the severe `erc.supply_short` rather
than `erc.multiply_driven_net`. Each must resolve to exactly ONE
electrical island: `erc.unconnected_net` fires on zero matches
(nothing in the layout carries that label at all) AND on more than
one (the rail is split into pieces that never touch) -- so ZERO
findings of that rule is exactly the 'one island per supply'
verdict, not merely an absence. The two Metal3 straps are the
design feature that makes each supply one island: without them
the 32 per-column M2 rail pairs would be 32 separate islands,
which is precisely the split-rail failure mode item 11 exists to
detect.
- There is deliberately NO `ties[]` section here, and that is a
recorded gap rather than an oversight: declaring one on a real
routed design collapses this layout into one electrical island
and reports a FALSE `erc.supply_short` -- filed upstream as
klayout-tools#2169 and reproduced four ways in gf180-drone-fc's
FRICTION F-034. Because `ties[]` is omitted, `erc.missing_tie` is
NOT COMPUTED by this run (klt erc's own contract: omitted
entirely -> never computed) -- a zero count is an absence of
evidence, not evidence of absence. The well-tie evidence that DOES
stand in for it, all already committed in this repo: (1)
layout/reports/lvs-array.json -- status `match`, with
VDD/VSS paired in net_correspondence (`pin: true`): the device-
aware netlist compare proves every transistor's supply terminal
reaches the named supply net; (2) layout/reports/extract-array.json
-- 16,706 extracted nets = 256 WL + 64 BL/BLB + 2 supply +
16,384 internal storage nodes: under full device-aware extraction
the supplies resolve to exactly ONE net each; (3) the bitcell's
own drawn taps -- a Pplus substrate tie strip and an Nplus-on-
Nwell strip (layout/bitcell/generate.py), DRC-clean against klt's
curated gf180mcu deck (layout/reports/drc-bitcell.json,
layout/reports/drc-array.json).
- Layer numbers derive from the PDK's own
libs.tech/klayout/tech/gf180mcu.lyp for gf180mcuD at open_pdks
commit c6d73a35f524070e5faff4a6a9eef49553ebc2b (this repo's
pinned revision -- sim/README.md) and cross-check against klt's
curated gf180mcu deck layer table and this GDS's own inventory:
Comp 22/0, Poly2 30/0, Contact 33/0, Metal1 34/0 (label 34/10),
Via1 35/0, Metal2 36/0, Via2 38/0, Metal3 42/0 (label 42/10);
three independent sources agree on every pair.
- `pdk` is left unset in the run (no --pdk): klt has no transcribed
gf180mcu antenna-ratio limit table (upstream calls gf180mcu
antenna limits a candidate follow-on), so per-gate antenna
verdicts read `unchecked`. That is not item 11's subject -- the
item's pass conditions are the erc findings above, and an antenna
or floating-gate verdict is a real defect that does NOT block
item 11 (klayout-tools#1994).
